passage:
At five, Samir stopped at the gate of Uday's birthday party and would not go in. He wrapped both arms around Mummy Damini's leg and hid his face in her kurta. When a grown-up said hello, Samir squeezed tighter. Mummy did not pull him off. She stood by the gate with a hand on his head until he peeked out at the balloons. Half an hour later he was sitting on the step with a paper hat.
At nine, Samir woke on the morning of the class play and curled up on his bed. "My tummy hurts," he said. Mummy Damini felt his forehead and let him stay home. Within an hour he was drawing on the floor, cheerful and calm. Two weeks later, the day before an oral test, his tummy hurt again, and this time the ache began the previous evening. Mummy noticed it came before things he dreaded. She sat beside him. "Something scary is coming up, isn't it?" Samir nodded. "If tummy aches keep happening, we'll also check with the doctor," she said, and they talked about what part of the test worried him.

qa.q: What did Samir do when a grown-up said hello at the party gate?
qa.a: He squeezed tighter around Mummy Damini's leg.

qa.q: How does Samir's stomach ache at nine connect to his hiding at the party at five?
qa.a: At five, hiding brought relief from what scared him. At nine, staying home from the class play made the fear drop at once, so the next time the ache started earlier, the night before the oral test, which shows that avoiding can grow.

qa.q: What was Samir feeling when he curled up on his bed on the morning of the class play?
qa.a: He was scared and worried about the play, and the tummy ache was how that fear showed up.

qa.q: What could Mummy Damini do next to help Samir face the test?
qa.a: She could keep asking what worries him, plan one small step with him, and check with the doctor if the tummy aches keep going.

grounding: A child hides behind a parent at a party and feels relief (3921); at nine a stomach ache and staying home give relief so the fear starts earlier (3286).
